_readme: THE APP #2 REHEARSAL'S STEPS, read by tooling/kit/rehearse-app2.mjs. [lane app2-dryrun, O-TIME-TO-SHIP-UNMEASURED]
Every step a second app takes from the brick to store-ready, in order. `auto`: run in the temporary work tree with {id},
{vars} and {tree} substituted, timed, pass or fail; `needs` names the tools it must find on PATH (a missing one is a SKIP,
which the runner reports as COVERAGE LOST, never as a pass). Each command is the kit's or a lane's own, in its dry-run
mode, and the same one ci.yml's stamp probe runs where it has one: the rehearsal adds no parallel path.
`manual`: a human, a console, a credential or a hand edit, with `row`, the register row that owns making it automatic, and
`estimateMinutes`, an estimate the time-to-ship fact sums (labelled an estimate in the output). An auto step with
`handEdits` that FAILS is manual too: the failing check is the evidence a person edits a file the kit should own (passing
untouched, it is automatic). A step may instead declare the one `refusal` it meets for a new app: the refusal's words
(`match`, a regex) and the `row` or `gate` that owns it. Web-prove-first ([pipeline 10]D-6) refuses every store submission
of a `preview` app by design: those steps are GATED, owned by the requirement. Any other failure is still a failure.
The kit's own readout (`new-product.mjs plan <id>`, the step marked `readout`) adds every
OWNER/NEXT/UNREAD step it names, mapped through `readoutRows`; a step it names that is not mapped there has NO ROW, and the
run exits 1 on it — that is a finding for the lead (a row or a lane), not a defect of this file.
`targets` says which of the seven targets (web, android, ios, macos, windows, linux, apps-gov-in) and the extension
template a step exercises; `unexercised` lists what a GitHub-hosted ubuntu runner cannot run, with the reason.

steps.name: plan before the stamp
stamp the app from the brick (one command)
site surface, catalogue and landing regenerated by the stamp
release tag filter owns the new app's tag
app declaration, privacy and legal generators
store tree on every channel
store listings in every language
sworn store declarations graded as preview
native platforms claimed only where built
analyze the stamped app
test the stamped app
web build
web bundle passes the deploy's fonts step
linux build (the one native target this runner compiles)
release builds compose for every native channel
brick Worker typechecks and passes its suite
erasure reaches the new Worker's database
backup and D1 fan-out sets include the new database
steps.why: A new app database reaches the nightly backup and the renewals fan-out only through an appWorkers row typed into the platform register, then render-platform-app-block.mjs.

steps.name: submitter dry run: Google Play

refusal.match: has status "preview" and only "live" may be submitted
refusal.why: Web-prove-first refuses every store submission of an app that is not live on the web: a deliberate gate, owned by the requirement, not a step to automate. Its cost is calendar time (the app must first convert strangers on the web), which this estimate leaves out.

steps.name: submitter dry run: App Store (iOS)

refusal.why: The App Store submitter refuses an app with no Apple identity: an App Store Connect record is a console step (owner O-A4), read back into app.yaml stores.

steps.name: extension template stamps (dry run)
argv: A rehearsal of the extension template.

steps.name: the kit's readout after the stamp
E2E lane targets the new app
steps.why: the nightly E2E lane names its one app by hand; a second app is wired by editing the workflow

steps.name: store submission lanes take the new app
steps.why: the submit-*.yml lanes hard-code the one app

steps.name: CI and Worker lanes name the new app
steps.why: lanes enumerate apps and Workers by hand

steps.name: Worker deploy job for the new app
steps.why: deploy-workers.yml carries a hand-copied job per Worker

steps.name: screenshot capture for the new app
steps.why: store-screenshots.yml and its driver name one app, and the brick stamps no capture suite

steps.name: native sign-in callback for the new app
steps.why: no native auth callback is built for an app the brick stamps

steps.name: Apple record, signing and submission
steps.why: an App Store Connect record, certificates and a profile are a console and a credential

readoutLanes._why: A readout step a scheduled workflow already does for every declared app is automated, not manual: name-clearance.yml re-derives apps/<app>/name-clearance.json weekly for every app in catalog/apps.json and lands it by pull request.

unexercised.why: the release build is composed (--print) but not compiled: the Android release build runs in build-platforms.yml, a release lane, and signing needs the upload key, a credential
iOS builds need a macOS runner and Apple signing; the rehearsal composes the ipa build and runs the App Store submitter's dry run only
macOS builds need a macOS runner; composed and dry-run submitted only
Windows builds need a Windows runner; composed and dry-run submitted only
the portal has no API (an owner upload); the apk build is composed and the store tree graded
